headline: BOJ deputy governor warns of market correction risk from AI boom
body: Bank of Japan deputy governor Shinichi Uchida said on Oct 5 the AI boom, "a big positive demand shock," may have eased financial conditions by boosting demand and asset prices. He said "there is a risk of correction if profits do not follow," and that bond issuance by AI firms is pushing up long-term rates. The BOJ has identified robust AI-related demand as a factor that could push underlying inflation above its 2% target.
note: A central bank naming AI-linked bond issuance as a force on long-term yields means lenders and investors exposed to the AI buildout should expect that link to show up in the next rate decision as well as the next earnings call.
correction: An earlier version stated as fact that the AI boom eased financial conditions and dropped "underlying" from the BOJ's inflation measure; Uchida said it may have done so, and the BOJ's concern is underlying inflation.

evidence.text: TOKYO – Bank of Japan (BOJ) deputy governor Shinichi Uchida said the global AI boom may have eased financial conditions by stoking demand and boosting asset prices, but warned of the risk of a market pullback if expected profits fail to materialise.
Referring to global AI adoption in an Oct 5 speech on the central bank’s website, Uchida described it as “a big positive demand shock, which has put upward pressure on the economy and prices”.
“Tentatively, it appears the demand side has come first and made financial conditions more accommodative on balance,” Uchida said. “But there is a risk of correction if profits do not follow.”
While artificial intelligence has boosted stock prices and made financial conditions easier, huge bond issuance by AI-related firms has put upward pressure on long-term interest rates, Uchida said.
The BOJ has identified robust AI-related demand as among factors that could push underlying inflation above its 2% target, necessitating further monetary tightening.
